issues.claim: `NeighbourhoodRequest` and `NeighbourhoodResult` are declared nowhere. V01 §2.4 (l. 516) says they "are II.1's (item 539)"; base II.1 (l. 18002) says they, "with DistrictContext and TypedBoundary, are V01 §2.4's"; V05 §2.3 (l. 385) cites "the `NeighbourhoodRequest` of V01 §2.4". The archive's declarations (V01 §2.4, the interface file f item 539 puts in II.1 in place of the base's old one, PIPELINE-0642/0643) are gone: the request's `district`, `key`, `layer`, `boundary`, `seam?`, `context?`, `laid {blocks, plots, alleys}`, `strategy?`, `params?`, `closeup?`, `outlineTemplate?`, `lod: 'neighbourhood'` and the result's `mode`, `blocks`, `ways`, `plots`, `buildings`, `greens`, `pins`, `hoodPins`, `places`, `labels`, `seams`, `report`, `districts`. The base comment also misattributes `TypedBoundary`, which §2.5 declares (l. 1082).
issues.required_change: II.1 declares, beside `NeighbourhoodStrategy`, `interface NeighbourhoodRequest { district: Id; key: PlatKey; layer: 'ground'|'sky'|'underground'; boundary: TypedBoundary; seam?: SeamContract; context?: DistrictContext; laid: { blocks: Id[]; plots: Id[]; alleys: Id[] }; strategy?: FabricStrategyId; params?: Record<string, number>; closeup?: CloseupParams; outlineTemplate?: OutlineTemplateId; lod: 'neighbourhood' }` and `interface NeighbourhoodResult { mode: 'refine'|'replace'|'unit'; blocks: Block[]; ways: Way[]; plots: Plot[]; buildings: Building[]; greens: Greenery[]; pins: Pin[]; hoodPins: HoodPin[]; places: HoodPlace[]; labels: LabelEntity[]; seams: SeamReport; report: StageReport; districts: Id[] }` with the archive's field comments (V01 §2.4 of the archive); the comment after it reads "`DistrictContext` is V01 §2.3's, `TypedBoundary` §2.5's"; V01 §2.4 keeps its pointer.

issues.claim: Item 114 (c) withdraws item 260's held deletion ("deleting one is for now"; it lapses at the next change that re-reads the kind — an epoch, a New random over a place it crossed, a Re-derive of the stage that builds it) and gives the off switch the "never" job. V01 still states the withdrawn rule: §0 l. 76 "remove one the generator raised (it stays removed)"; §3.17.5 (1) "a removal of a generated part is a suppression, item 260, that holds through regeneration" and (2) "the suppression's one reader … a Re-derive from S4 or S6 lays no raised part where one holds"; §1b l. 179 ("supports, spans and suppression"); §4's tool row l. 2590 ("a removal's suppression, item 260"); T-V1-52 "the viaduct stays absent after Regenerate (keep), after New random on each crossed district and after a Re-derive from S6".

T-V1-52: "the viaduct stays absent after a plain Regenerate and a reload; after New random on a crossed district, a Re-derive from S6 or one epoch the generator may lay one again, and the deleted one counts against no cap; with raised ways switched off none is laid (item 114 (e))".
